note: Caching behaviour (minimum cacheable prefix, TTLs, refresh semantics, what is billed) read from each provider's official documentation on last_verified. Prices live in data/pricing.json. Do not edit a number here from memory — re-verify on docs_url first.

providers.label: Anthropic Claude API
providers.control_note: Cache breakpoints are explicit: a `cache_control` block marks the end of the cached prefix. Automatic caching (one top-level `cache_control`) is also available.
providers.refresh_quote: The cache is refreshed for no additional cost each time the cached content is used.
providers.break_even_quote: A cache hit costs 10% of the standard input price, which means caching pays off after one cache read for the 5-minute duration (1.25x write), or after two cache reads for the 1-hour duration (2x write).
providers.below_minimum_quote: Shorter prompts cannot be cached, even if marked with `cache_control`. Any requests to cache fewer than this number of tokens will be processed without caching, and no error is returned.
providers.breakpoint_hint: Place `cache_control` on the last block whose prefix is identical across the requests you want to share a cache.

providers.label: OpenAI API
providers.control_note: Caching is automatic: a repeated prefix is reused with no API change. GPT-5.6 and later also support explicit breakpoints.
providers.refresh_quote: A cached prefix remains eligible for reuse for 30 minutes after its most recent write or reuse.
providers.break_even_quote: For GPT-5.6 and later, cache writes cost 1.25x the standard, uncached input-token rate; cache reads cost only 0.1x that rate. Earlier models incur no additional cache-write charge.
providers.below_minimum_quote: The minimum cacheable prompt length is 1,024 tokens for GPT-5.6 and later and 2,048 tokens for models older than GPT-5.6.
providers.breakpoint_hint: Put stable developer instructions and shared reference material first; any change before a breakpoint stops the rest of the prefix from matching.

providers.label: Google Gemini API
providers.control_note: Implicit caching is on by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer; explicit caches are created with a TTL and are the only mode you can plan around. Cached tokens are billed at the context-caching rate, plus storage for as long as the cache lives.
providers.refresh_quote: If not set, the TTL defaults to 1 hour. (Nothing in the docs extends an explicit cache's lifetime when it is read, so the model here recreates the cache once per TTL window.)
providers.break_even_quote: Billing is based on the following factors: Cache token count: the number of input tokens cached, billed at a reduced rate when included in subsequent prompts. Storage duration: the amount of time cached tokens are stored (TTL), billed based on the TTL duration of cached token count.
providers.below_minimum_quote: The minimum input token count for context caching varies by model. The maximum is the same as the maximum for the given model.
providers.breakpoint_hint: Try putting large and common contents at the beginning of your prompt, and send requests with a similar prefix in a short amount of time.
